title: 1973 AHSME Problem 10
statement: If \(n\) is a real number, then the simultaneous system \[ \begin{cases} nx+y=1,\\ ny+z=1,\\ x+nz=1 \end{cases} \] has no solution if and only if \(n\) is equal to

solutions.text:
Adding the equations gives \[ (n+1)(x+y+z)=3. \] When \(n=-1,\) this becomes \(0=3,\) so no solution exists. If \(n\ne-1,\) the symmetric assignment \[ x=y=z=\frac1{n+1} \] satisfies all three equations. Hence the system has no solution exactly when \(n=-1.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Add all three equations and inspect the coefficient of \(x+y+z\)
For every remaining value of \(n,\) try the symmetric choice \(x=y=z\)
